verdict.line: You lose if you keep trading into Mordekaiser's longer-ranged Obliterate and let Darkness Rise and Death's Grasp force all-ins before level 6; you win if you farm safely through Spirit Fire's zone and arrive at a stacked Siphoning Strike with Trinity Force before he can close the lane out.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's Q (Obliterate, 675 range) outreaches your Q (Siphoning Strike, 255 range) by nearly 3x, so he can poke and shove without ever walking into your true damage window. His passive (Darkness Rise) rewards him for landing three hits in a trade, and his W (Indestructible) banks both damage dealt and taken into a shield he can convert into healing - every short trade you take funds his sustain. Your path to parity is farming through the deficit: stack Siphoning Strike, shred his armor with Spirit Fire, and let Trinity Force close the gap he opened early.

theirWindow.when: he lands his third hit on you
theirWindow.what: Darkness Rise procs, giving him a damage aura and bonus move speed - disengage immediately and let the wave or terrain separate you rather than exchanging again.

yourWindow.what: He has no pull to start an all-in, so step up safely to land Siphoning Strike on the wave, drop Spirit Fire, or take a free poke.

start.why: The sustain and poke-reduction (49.3% WR over 1622 games, 64.9% pick) absorb Obliterate's free-range chip damage without forcing you to recall early.

boots.why: 51.8% WR over 1240 games and the most-picked option (51.7%); lower Q/W/E cooldowns mean more Siphoning Strikes per back-and-forth and more frequent Spirit Fire zoning.

core.why: The 62.9% WR path (264 games) that converts your stacked Q damage and movement speed into real threat the moment you hit it.
Magic-damage sustain against Morde's Obliterate/Death's Grasp poke, and it amplifies the lifesteal from your own Soul Eater passive.
Armor and attack-speed slow that blunts his melee trades once he's forced to stand next to you post-Death's Grasp.

situational.when: mordekaiser is ahead and poking you down from range before you can close in
he's leaning on indestructible's stored-damage heal to win extended fights
he or his team starts stacking healing or lifesteal to outlast your damage

runes.keystoneWhy: The move-speed burst and healing let you disengage out of Obliterate's range after a short trade instead of standing in it and feeding his passive.

summoners.why: This pairing posts the best measured win rate (51.9% over 26.3% pick); Flash dodges a Death's Grasp pull and Ghost lets you close distance to stack Q or disengage once Wither has slowed him.

playing.title: Farm with Q, don't duel
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike's 255 range means you're already inside Obliterate's 675 range when you use it - only step up to use it when his Q is visibly on cooldown.

playing.title: Zone waves with Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Drop E on the minion wave before he walks up to trade; the armor reduction boosts every auto and Q you land on him while he's in it.

playing.title: Save Wither for his engage
playing.detail: Wither slows both move and attack speed over time - hold it to peel after a Death's Grasp pull, or to run him down once your stacks make you the stronger duelist.

playing.title: Disengage on third hit
playing.detail: The instant Darkness Rise procs on him, back off the trade; continuing to swing into his buffed damage and speed is how these lanes get lost.

playing.title: Track Death's Grasp cooldown
playing.detail: It's 16s at rank 1, falling to 8s by rank 5 - after he pulls or whiffs it, that's your safe window to farm or poke until it's back up.

playing.title: Don't feed his shield
playing.detail: Indestructible banks damage dealt and taken into a heal - avoid throwing out autos or Q when he's clearly disengaging, since you're just funding his sustain for free.

playing.title: Play for the level 11+ spike
playing.detail: Trinity Force plus a stacked Q is your win condition per the data (62.9% WR, 264 games) - look to convert to side-lane plates and turret pressure once itemized rather than forcing earlier skirmishes.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1); the tactical reasoning connecting them to the Nasus-vs-Mordekaiser mechanics is my own read, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance from Mordekaiser to prevent his (P) from activating. Focus on raising [Q] stacks while keeping Mordekaiser’s skills in mind. Focus on farming with [Q] and growing while waiting for an opportunity.
